name: West Bengal
summary_text: West Bengal replicates the Tripura checkpoint script: South Dinajpur police arrested a Bangladeshi transgender person for allegedly "infiltrating India," treating trans presentation as evidence of illegal entry rather than identity; police also detained the e-rickshaw driver who carried her from the border. The state shares a long Bangladesh border and falls within the same policing logic. West Bengal is also one of only three states recording cases under the Transgender Persons Act in 2021 (3 of 7 nationally), indicating some legal infrastructure exists but also that trans-targeted crime is occurring at a detectable rate. Against the national 0.43, West Bengal sits −0.09. The border profiling is visitor-facing and state-actor-driven, but the incidents are fewer and less concentrated than Tripura's repeated-sweep pattern. Compared to Tripura (0.31), West Bengal's harm is a single documented arrest plus the broader infiltration framing rather than repeated mass operations; compared to Delhi (0.38), which shares the profiling language but also has India's strongest institutional trans presence, West Bengal lacks that offsetting civic infrastructure outside Kolkata. A welfare board exists (one of 12 states/UTs with a constituted body), but per the RTI investigation it operates without a functioning policy framework. For a foreign visitor transiting the land border, the primary exposure is the same appearance-as-suspicion-trigger mechanism documented in Tripura.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (access-denied block); the underlying East Bengal report covers South Dinajpur police arresting "Ali Mondal aka Bijli Mondal," a Bangladeshi transgender person from Sirajganj district, for allegedly infiltrating India, along with the e-rickshaw driver who brought her across the border.

sources.title: India’s crime data would have you believe that trans people barely face any violence—here’s why that doesn’t add up - Queerbeat
sources.claim_summary: Queerbeat analysis of India's official hate-crime data: NCRB totals make trans violence nearly invisible through under-reporting and misclassification; among its usable figures, West Bengal was one of only three states recording any Transgender Persons Act cases in 2021 — 3 of the 7 cases nationwide.

sources.title: Constitution of Transgender Welfare Boards/Commissions
sources.claim_summary: Press Information Bureau, Government of India (8 Dec 2021, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment): state-wise list of the 12 states/UTs that had constituted Transgender Welfare Boards under the Transgender Persons Rules 2020 — West Bengal included. Official record of the board's existence.

sources.title: The Reality of Transgender Welfare Boards in India: An RTI Investigation
sources.claim_summary: The Quint RTI investigation (5 Nov 2024) into state Transgender Welfare Boards: most constituted boards are "rudderless," without compliance mechanism or real power — the basis for treating West Bengal's board as nominal.
